Mukesh S/o Babu Lal, R/o Ruparali, P.s. Salamgarh, Dist.
 Pratapgarh
----Respondents For Appellant(s) : Mr. Hemank Vaishnav
For Respondent(s) : Mr. S.S. Rajpurohit, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR GARG Order 15/03/2024
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Public Prosecutor and perused the material available on record.

The instant criminal fourth appeal has been filed under Section 14 A (2) of SC/ST Act on behalf of the appellant, who is in custody in connection with FIR No.128/2021, Police Station Salamgarh,
District Pratapgarh for the offences under Section 365, 366, 343, 370, 376(1) & 120-B IPC and Section 3(2)(VA) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and against the order dated 20.10.2023 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities Act) Cases, Pratapgarh whereby the bail application preferred under Section 439 Cr.P.C. on behalf of the appellant was rejected.

entities.text: Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities Act) Cases, Pratapgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The earlier appeal was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 29.05.2023.

It has been submitted on behalf of the appellant that the prosecutrix has been examined in the Court as PW/4 and in her cross examination, she specifically mentioned that she roamed [2024:RJ-JD:12323] (2 of 2) [CRLAS-2590/2023] around with the appellant at so many places at her own free will and during this time she did not raise any hue and cry.
Counsel further submits that similar situated co-accused has already been granted bail.

The accused-appellant is in judicial custody since 14.07.2021 and upto this time only seven prosecution witnesses have been examined Gyarsi Lal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:12323) on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41043739/

entities.text: Gyarsi Lal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:12323)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 out of 14 of list of witnesses and the trial of the case will take sufficient long time to be concluded.
Therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-appellant.
Learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the prayer for bail.

Having regard to the entirety of facts and circumstances as available on record and upon a consideration of the arguments advanced at the bar, this Court is of the opinion that the order rejecting the application for bail filed on behalf of the appellant, cannot be sustained and deserves to be set aside.
Consequently, the instant appeal criminal fourth appeal is allowed.
The impugned order dated 20.10.2023 passed by learned Special Judge SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities Act) Cases, Pratapgarh is set aside.

entities.text: Special Judge SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities Act) Cases, Pratapgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is ordered that the accused-appellant Gyarsi Lal S/o Banna Ram @ Manna Ram arrested in connection with FIR No.128/2021, Police Station Salamgarh, District Pratapgarh shall be released on bail; provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- and two sureties bond of Rs.50,000/- to the satisfaction of the learned trial court with the stipulation to appear before that court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 74-Ishan/-
